Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Civic life: news, government & the law

private adjective

not public

also privately owned, private life, private property, private school, private citizen

classical

Caes. BG 4.1: nihil prīvātī ac sēparātī agrī (Lewis & Short)
Quint. 1.2.1
Traupman 365

prīvātus, prīvāta, prīvātum

adjective

private, of one person, not of the state

Of one person, against pūblicus and commūnis (Lewis & Short): rēs prīvātae, private property (Cic. Quinct. 15); vīta prīvāta, a life away from public affairs (Cic. Sen. 22). As a noun, a private citizen (see individual).

Examples

  • ūtiliusne sit domī atque intrā prīvātōs parietēs studentem continēre an frequentiae scholārum … trādere

    whether it is better to keep the pupil at home, within private walls, or to hand him over to the crowd of the schoolsQuint. 1.2.1

  • ex quō togam virīlem sūmpsit nūllō diē prius ūllam pūblicam prīvātamque rem ēgit quam in Capitōlium īret

    from the day he came of age he never did any business, public or private, before going up to the CapitolLiv. 26.19.5

See also individual, own, private, personal.

SourcesLewis & Short: privatus · Lewis & Short: publicus
